title: Self-Supervised Flow Matching for Scalable Multi-Modal Synthesis
claim: Our method reaches baseline quality in far fewer training steps and yields visibly better samples than the vanilla baseline.
layout: 2 panels: left convergence line plot, right paired sample grids; arrow marks speedup
description: The figure has two parts. Panel (a) on the left is a line plot of text-to-image FID against training steps from 200K to 1M. A blue REPA curve flattens near 3.92. An orange Self-Flow curve (ours) falls steadily to about 3.6. A dashed gray horizontal line marks the vanilla flow matching result at 1M steps. A black double-headed arrow labeled '2.8x faster' shows how much sooner Self-Flow reaches REPA's final quality. Panel (b) on the right is a grid of generated samples, with Flow Matching columns beside Self-Flow columns. The left pair shows a parrot and fingernails spelling 'LOVE'. The right pair shows three video frames of a woman doing push-ups, with a downward 'Time' arrow. Italic prompts sit under each sample group. The eye goes first to the plot's gap between the curves, then to the photos.
caption: Results obtained by our self-supervised flow matching framework, Self-Flow. (a) On text-to-image generation, our method converges $\sim2.8\times$ faster than REPA [ref], the predominant external-alignment method, without using any external models or supervision. Notably, REPA plateaus while our method continues to improve. (b) Compared to vanilla flow matching, our approach improves structural coherence, text rendering, and temporal consistency.
abstract: Strong semantic representations improve the convergence and generation quality of diffusion and flow models. Existing approaches largely rely on external models, which require separate training, operate on misaligned objectives, and exhibit unexpected scaling behavior. We argue that this dependence arises from the model's training objective, which poses a denoising task with little incentive to learn semantic representations. We introduce Self-Flow: a self-supervised flow matching paradigm that integrates representation learning within the generative framework. Our key mechanism, Dual-Timestep Scheduling, applies heterogeneous noise levels across tokens, creating an information asymmetry that forces the model to infer missing information from corrupted inputs. This drives learning strong representations alongside generative capabilities without external supervision. Our method generalizes across modalities and enables multi-modal training while following expected scaling laws, achieving superior image, video, and audio generation.
